rationale: C22 plausibly supplied the child’s central government-wide administrative template: department and agency heads must pursue maximum effectiveness and economy; the Bureau of the Budget advises and assists them; agencies report progress; and the Bureau reports to the President. The child materially reuses this machinery while narrowing it to personnel and adding the Civil Service Commission. C09 and C20 provide relevant personnel/mobilization context, but neither matches the child’s full operative sequence as closely.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I expect the head of each executive department and agency to take all necessary actions to conserve manpower and generally to bring about maximum effectiveness and economy in the utilization of personnel.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Department and agency heads shall (a) review the programs under their respective jurisdictions to assure themselves and the President that such programs are being carried out with maximum effectiveness and economy
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive shared formulation assigns all agency heads responsibility for achieving “maximum effectiveness and economy,” adapted in the child specifically to personnel utilization.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I want you, together with the Chairman of the Civil Service Commission, to issue instructions on steps which can be taken to conserve manpower, and to advise and consult with the departments and agencies
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The Bureau of the Budget shall ... advise and assist the agencies in working out programs to improve their operations
shared_material.explanation: Both give the Bureau of the Budget a government-wide advisory and assistance role supporting agency implementation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Bureau of the Budget and the Civil Service Commission [shall] request reports from all departments and agencies and conduct regular inspections and surveys so that reports can be made to me on progress
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Department and agency heads shall ... report periodically to the Bureau of the Budget on the progress made ... [and the Bureau shall] report periodically to the President on the progress and results
shared_material.explanation: The child preserves the parent’s two-stage progress-reporting machinery—from agencies to the Bureau and from the Bureau to the President—while adding inspections, surveys, and Civil Service Commission participation.
